newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close lower ahead of fresh supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close lower ahead of fresh supply.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ended slightly lower in dull, lackluster trade as major players were mostly sidelined ahead of upcoming fresh supply, analysts said.
The 6-1/2-percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond ended down 3/32 at 100-13/32 to yield 6.47 percent. The two-year note was off 1/32 at 100-11/32, yielding 5.68 percent.

"In terms of flows, it's really kind of dead ... But we saw a few players buying three-year (notes) and selling twos and fives that will be auctioned this week," said a senior trader at a major U.S. investment bank.

The Treasury will offer the market $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year securities on Wednesday. The bidding deadlines for the auctions are set at 1300 EST/1700 GMT.
Prices traded in very narrow ranges throughout the session as the market remained in a consolidation mood after a recent rally tied to the notion the economy is slowing with no signs of inflation.
"I think what's going on ... is a lot of soul searching to see if these yield levels are appropriate for now," said Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets Inc.
The U.S. Treasury market rallied sharply over the last two weeks, sending the yield on the bellwether 30-year bond to its lowest levels in eight months.

Analysts said activity was very thin on Monday. They added portfolio managers, hedge and pension funds were mostly out of the market. Some traders reported scant retail participation in the long-end of the curve.
The short-end of the yield curve was particularly slow. By 1630 EST/2130 GMT, volume in the bill sector of the yield curve as measured by GovPX was $18.3 billion, around nine percent below average.

Turnover in coupons was $33.5 billion, eight percent below the daily average. GovPX publishes real-time Treasury prices and volume from five of the six intra-dealer brokers, representing 65 percent of the intra-dealers trades.
"The day was very quiet here, very boring," said Maureen Mooney, senior fixed-income research specialist at GovPX.

Analysts said the dearth of fresh economic indicators is likely to continue to take a toll on the market later in the week. "We're still bullish on this market," said the head of the Treasury desk at a foreign investment bank here.
"But I think some people might use the supply and the lack of key data as an excuse to take some profits over the next few days," the trader added.

The economic calendar is very light this week. Analysts said the market will be mostly bracing for the release of the housing starts report for October on Tuesday and the September international trade on Wednesday.
"There isn't much data between now and Thanksgiving (on November 28). So we're likely to see more profit-taking perhaps and some deep thinking," HSBC's Low said.
The three-month Treasury bill rate closed up one basis point at 5.02 percent. The six-month bill rate was up one point at 5.06 percent. The year bill rate was up one point at 5.12 percent.

The two-year note closed off 1/32 at 100-11/32, yielding 5.68 percent. The five-year note traded down 2/32 at 101-6/32 to yield 5.97 percent. The ten-year note closed down 3/32 at 102-6/32, yielding 6.20 percent.
